title: Research & Impact | IHM School of Social Work
desc: Practice-based social work research, publications and global partnerships at the IHM School of Social Work, Melbourne.

blocks.t: Knowledge that moves with the world.

blocks.p: Practice-based research, global perspectives and scholarship that strengthens social work.

blocks.alt: Social work researchers collaborating around a table

img.alt: Guest lecture on person-centred care in the age of AI at IHM

blocks.p: IHM has established a sustainable and growing research culture, underpinned by its Research and Innovation Hub and Research and Scholarship Committee, under the leadership of Dr Balasankar Ganesan.

Academic leadership of the BSW is provided by Professor Abraham Francis, Head of School, Social Work, with over 30 years of experience in social work education, practice, research and international collaboration.

blocks.t: Research in progress and in print

blocks.p: Our academics work across gender-based violence, men and masculinities, workplace safety, multiculturalism, disability, mental health, digital healthcare, social policy and social development.

blocks.p: IHM’s collaboration with Arizona State University through the Cintana Education Alliance integrates ASU-developed digital resources, curricula and online modules into our programs, providing global mobility pathways and contemporary pedagogical approaches including technology-enhanced learning and competency-based education.

partners: Australian Council of Heads of Social Work Education

IHM’s membership helps keep the Social Work program aligned with national best practice and connected to the collective expertise of social work education leaders. Students benefit from curriculum informed by national dialogue on workforce needs, placement quality and industry expectations.
Australian & New Zealand Social Work & Welfare Education and Research

This trans-Tasman network connects IHM with social work educators and researchers, helping the program remain research-informed and responsive to emerging practice trends across Australia and New Zealand.
International Association of Schools of Social Work

IASSW membership connects students and academics to the global social work community, international best practice, human rights frameworks and global social policy dialogue, while opening pathways to conferences and collaborative research.

This partnership strengthens real-world field education connections across community services, NGOs and welfare organisations, helping students build practical experience, professional relationships and confidence before graduation.
Congress of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Nurses and Midwives

The relationship brings community-led expertise in Indigenous health and wellbeing into IHM’s institutional knowledge and curriculum design, strengthening cultural safety, reconciliation commitments and community accountability.
National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Ageing and Aged Care Council

This connection provides guidance on the cultural, spiritual and community dimensions of ageing well for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and supports culturally appropriate aged care knowledge.

The partnership helps embed truth-telling, respect and partnership principles into institutional culture and creates channels for continuing dialogue with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander leaders.

Willum Warrain gives IHM a trusted connection to community life and community-led service delivery, bringing direct insight from community members and Elders into Social Work education and engagement.
This relationship connects IHM with culturally grounded advocacy and service-delivery approaches designed by and for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
Council of Academic Public Health Institutions Australasia
CAPHIA connects institutions engaged in public health education, strengthening sector dialogue, academic exchange and contemporary approaches to population wellbeing.
Higher Education Private Provider Quality Network
Participation supports shared learning and quality-focused dialogue across Australia’s independent higher education sector.
The association supports connection with public health knowledge, policy discussion and professional networks relevant to community wellbeing and social work practice.
IEAA engagement supports internationally informed education, sector connection and better experiences for globally mobile students.
AIDH connects IHM with digital health thinking and professional exchange relevant to technology-enabled, person-centred care.
ITECA provides sector connection and representation across independent skills training, higher education and international education.
Gold affiliate status reflects IHM’s continuing commitment to professional connection, sector participation and quality education.
